module_title: Delhi Sultanate - Economy, Theory of Kingship, and Decline
introduction: This advanced level provides an analytical study of the Iqta system, the politics of the 'Turkan-i-Chahalgani', Balban's Theory of Kingship, the Sultanate taxation system, and Firoz Shah Tughlaq's orthodox yet welfare-oriented state.

core_concepts.title: Iqta System
core_concepts.description: Institutionalized by Iltutmish, it was a land-grant system where officers (Muqtis/Walis) were given the right to collect revenue from a territory (Iqta) in lieu of a cash salary. They maintained troops from this revenue and remitted the surplus (Fawazil) to the Sultan.

core_concepts.title: Turkan-i-Chahalgani (The Corps of Forty)
core_concepts.description: Iltutmish created a ruling elite consisting of his 40 most loyal slave-nobles. After his death, they became powerful 'kingmakers'. Eventually, Balban (who was once a member himself) crushed this group to restore the crown's prestige.

core_concepts.title: Balban's Theory of Kingship
core_concepts.description: Balban adopted the policy of 'Blood and Iron'. He declared the Sultan as the shadow of God on earth ('Zill-i-Ilahi') and introduced Persian court customs like 'Sijda' (prostration) and 'Paibos' (kissing the monarch's feet) to establish absolute authority.

core_concepts.title: Sultanate Taxation System
core_concepts.description: Based on Islamic law (Sharia), there were 4 main taxes: 1. Kharaj (land tax on non-Muslims), 2. Ushr (land tax on Muslims), 3. Jizya (religious tax on non-Muslims), 4. Zakat (religious tax on Muslims). 'Khums' was the tax on war booty.

core_concepts.title: Firoz Shah Tughlaq (FST) and the Welfare State
core_concepts.description: FST built the largest network of irrigation canals and founded new cities (Hisar, Firozabad, Jaunpur). He established 'Diwan-i-Khairat' (charity department) and 'Diwan-i-Bandagan' (department of slaves - he maintained around 1.8 lakh slaves).

important_entities.name: Ghiyasuddin Balban
important_entities.significance: Reorganized the military department (Diwan-i-Arz) to defend against the Mongols and introduced the Persian New Year festival 'Navroz' in India.

important_entities.name: Amir Khusrau
important_entities.significance: A great Sufi musician and poet who witnessed the reign of 7 different Sultans. He is credited with the invention of the Sitar and Tabla, and is considered the first poet of Khari Boli (early Hindi).

important_entities.name: Timur Lang (1398 AD)
important_entities.significance: Invaded Delhi during the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud (Tughlaq dynasty). His devastating massacre and plunder broke the back of the Delhi Sultanate, paving the way for the Sayyid dynasty.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Initially, Brahmins, women, and children were exempt from paying the Jizya tax. However, Firoz Shah Tughlaq became the first Sultan to impose Jizya strictly on Brahmins as well.
Students often confuse who destroyed the Corps of Forty. Iltutmish 'created' it, whereas Balban 'destroyed' it to centralize his own power.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Both Diwan-i-Bandagan (for slaves) and Diwan-i-Khairat (for orphans/widows) were set up by Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

exam_strategy_tips: In Assertion-Reasoning questions, deeply analyze the relationship between Balban's severe 'Theory of Kingship' and his motive to destroy the Turkan-i-Chahalgani.
Questions asking to match taxation terms (Kharaj, Jizya, Zakat, Khums) to their respective definitions are a staple in UPSC and State Civil Services exams.
